escena: SCENE (a staged piece for a campaign, shot inside the agency's own creative studio — a large, deliberately designed space, not an office): the room has SCALE and EMPTINESS, and that is what makes it expensive. Ceiling height of two floors, a polished concrete floor with a soft wet-looking sheen that carries faint reflections, and a full-height INDUSTRIAL WINDOW WALL of slim matte-black steel mullions running down the LEFT side, its panes filled with cool daylight. Far behind her, a GALLERY WALL: a grid of large printed pieces of the agency's own work, pinned in perfect alignment on a pale plaster wall, with no legible words at this distance. 🔵 THE WORK ITSELF CARRIES THE BRAND BLUE: several of those prints are dominated by large flat fields of deep ACTIVE BLUE rgb(3,117,219), so the grid reads as a rhythm of blue blocks across the back of the room — the blue is IN THE WORK, a real printed surface, never a painted backdrop and never a filter. One more blue field lies on the oak table, a large proof seen at a grazing angle. Between her and that wall, a long solid OAK worktable with a few printed sheets squared up on it and nothing else — the luxury is how little there is. Nothing is cluttered, nothing is decorative: no plants, no bookshelves, no sofas, no coffee cups, no domestic objects of any kind. SOMETHING IS HAPPENING, and it is a small, precise act — this is a moment, not a pose. Nexa is JUDGING A PROOF: she holds a single large printed sheet with both hands at chest height, fingertips light on its two upper corners, and has tilted it a few degrees INTO the window light to read how the ink sits on the paper — the movement of someone checking a colour, not someone displaying an object. Her body is turned THREE QUARTERS towards the window on her left, so the FRONT of the jacket faces the camera and its embroidered chest mark is fully visible; her back is never square to the lens. She has just lifted her eyes from the sheet to the camera, chin level, with a small closed-lip smile of quiet satisfaction — poised, unhurried, exact: everything about her reads as care and craft. She LOOKS STRAIGHT INTO THE LENS. Her posture is elegant and still: shoulders down and level, neck long, spine straight, weight settled on one leg, elbows close to the body. Her hands are the second subject of this picture: long fingers, relaxed, holding the paper by its very edge the way someone handles work that matters. 🟠 THE ACCENT IS BORN OF THE TASK, never decoration: a roll of ORANGE rgb(245,93,1) marking tape sits pushed up on her left wrist like a bracelet, and a short torn strip of the same orange tape marks the corner of the proof she is holding — the only warm colour in the room, a few percent of the frame at most, there because she is working. Her head stays FRONTAL: both eyes and both eyebrows fully visible, both cheeks visible, the bridge of her nose does not cut across either cheek. Her irises are VERY DARK BROWN, almost black, so dark that the iris barely separates from the pupil — never hazel, amber or honey, and no golden ring. She wears the Efeonce softshell jacket, open, over a plain dark tee. CRITICAL ON LIGHT, and every practical lamp is SWITCHED OFF: the KEY is the WINDOW itself, hard directional daylight from the LEFT raking across her, throwing the long shadows of the steel mullions in clean diagonal bars across the concrete floor and along the base of the wall; those bars, the pools they make and the whole lit diagonal stay BELOW THE MIDDLE OF THE FRAME. The haze in the air makes the window light readable as volume. A single slim ACTIVE BLUE rgb(3,117,219) architectural LED strip is recessed at the base of the gallery wall, far behind her and low, washing a thin band of brand blue up that wall — blue as ARCHITECTURAL LIGHT, never paint and never a backdrop. 🔴 HER SKIN STAYS NEUTRAL: the daylight on her face is white, so her skin, the jacket and the tee read in TRUE NEUTRAL COLOUR, never blue-cast, never cyan; the blue lives only in that far band and in the faint reflection it leaves on the polished floor. THREE PLANES: the out-of-focus black edge of a flight case at the very front; Nexa sharp in the near third; the table, the gallery wall and the depth of the room behind. She stands LOW: the very top of her head — and the top of her raised arm — are at or BELOW 38% of the frame height. The whole TOP THIRD of the picture is the tall upper wall DEEP IN SHADOW and the dark volume of the ceiling above the window's reach: it must read DARK, never as pale lit plaster, completely unbroken — no window bar, no blue band, no print, no lamp and no light patch may enter it. Everything is unbranded except her jacket. 85mm at f/2.8, focus on her eyes.

lecho.objeto: the black edge of a flight case standing right at the lens, its aluminium trim crossing the ENTIRE bottom of the frame from left edge to right edge, a hand's width from the camera and dissolved completely out of focus. It sits OUTSIDE the window light entirely, in the shadow the window frame leaves
lecho.tono: NEAR-BLACK and NEUTRAL, the darkest thing in the picture and even across its whole width, with NO blue cast and NO window bar falling on it — NOTHING else appears in that bottom strip: no hands, no floor reflection, no cable, no highlight, no lettering

texto.muro: the tall empty upper wall above the gallery grid, filling the top third

suspendido: a fine curl of dust lifted off the print she has just turned, caught in the window light and frozen in its drift
